subject: Error when adding new models (from CPC 2021 workshop)

messages.author: 4fbb3047244b71ab
messages.subject: Error when adding new models (from CPC 2021 workshop)
parts:
Dear all,

In CPC Reinforcement Learning Tutorial, I find hBayesDM could be a quite convenient toolbox. Thanks for your brilliant work! 

For now, I want to add a new model (a hybrid model for bandit2arm task) to fit my data. I checked out "How to add new model" page, and followed the steps. It seems OK ahead, but after I did step 7, installing my modified hBayesDM on R and testing it with example data, the package didn't work and reported that:

WARNING: empty program
no parameter mu_r, mu_beta, sigma, r, beta, log_lik; sampling not done
Stan model '' does not contain samples.

For this test, I didn't use my new model but a existing model (dd_exp), which works well if I remove my modified hBayesDM and install the original package through install.packages("hBayesDM").

Do you have any suggestions for this issue? Thanks a lot!

Best wishes,
Zijie

messages.subject: Re: Error when adding new models (from CPC 2021 workshop)
parts:
Dear Jaeyeong,

Here's my Stan file. To be honest I'm not familiar with Stan...

#include /pre/license.stan

data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> T;
  int<lower=1, upper=T> Tsubj[N];
  int<lower=-1, upper=2> choice[N, T];
  real outcome[N, T];  // no lower and upper bounds
}
transformed data {
  vector[2] initV;  // initial values for EV
  initV = rep_vector(0.5, 2);
}
parameters {
// Declare all parameters as vectors for vectorizing
  // Hyper(group)-parameters
  vector[4] mu_pr;
  vector<lower=0>[4] sigma;

  // Subject-level raw parameters (for Matt trick)
  vector[N] alpha_pr;    // attention
  vector[N] kappa_pr;    // constraint
  vector[N] eta_pr;    // weight
  vector[N] tau_pr;  // inverse temperature
}
transformed parameters {
  // subject-level parameters
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[N] alpha;
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[N] kappa;
  vector<lower=0, upper=1>[N] eta;
  vector<lower=0, upper=5>[N] tau;

  for (i in 1:N) {
    alpha[i]   = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1]  + sigma[1]  * alpha_pr[i]);
    kappa[i]   = Phi_approx(mu_pr[2]  + sigma[2]  * kappa_pr[i]);
    eta[i]   = Phi_approx(mu_pr[3]  + sigma[3]  * eta_pr[i]);
    tau[i] = Phi_approx(mu_pr[4] + sigma[4] * tau_pr[i]) * 5;
  }
}
model {
  // Hyperparameters
  mu_pr  ~ normal(0, 1);
  sigma ~ normal(0, 0.2);

  // individual parameters
  alpha_pr   ~ normal(0, 1);
  kappa_pr   ~ normal(0, 1);
  eta_pr   ~ normal(0, 1);
  tau_pr ~ normal(0, 1);

  // subject loop and trial loop
  for (i in 1:N) {
    vector[2] ev; // expected value
    real PE;      // prediction error

    ev = initV;

    for (t in 1:(Tsubj[i])) {
      // compute action probabilities
      choice[i, t] ~ categorical_logit(tau[i] * ev);

      // prediction error
      PE = outcome[i, t] - ev[choice[i, t]];

      // value updating (learning)
      ev[choice[i, t]] += kappa[i] * alpha[i] * PE;
      ev[3-choice[i, t]] = 1 - ev[choice[i, t]];
      alpha[i] = eta[i] * abs(PE) + (1 - eta[i]) * alpha[i];
    }
  }
}
generated quantities {
  // For group level parameters
  real<lower=0, upper=1> mu_alpha;
  real<lower=0, upper=1> mu_kappa;
  real<lower=0, upper=1> mu_eta;
  real<lower=0, upper=5> mu_tau;

  // For log likelihood calculation
  real log_lik[N];

  // For posterior predictive check
  real y_pred[N, T];

  // Set all posterior predictions to 0 (avoids NULL values)
  for (i in 1:N) {
    for (t in 1:T) {
      y_pred[i, t] = 0;
    }
  }

  mu_alpha   = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1]);
  mu_kappa   = Phi_approx(mu_pr[2]);
  mu_eta   = Phi_approx(mu_pr[3]);
  mu_tau = Phi_approx(mu_pr[4]) * 5;

  { // local section, this saves time and space
    for (i in 1:N) {
      vector[2] ev; // expected value
      real PE;      // prediction error

      // Initialize values
      ev = initV;

      log_lik[i] = 0;

      for (t in 1:(Tsubj[i])) {
        // compute log likelihood of current trial
        log_lik[i] += categorical_logit_lpmf(choice[i, t] | tau[i] * ev);

        // generate posterior prediction for current trial
        y_pred[i, t] = categorical_rng(softmax(tau[i] * ev));

        // prediction error
        PE = outcome[i, t] - ev[choice[i, t]];

        // value updating (learning)
        ev[choice[i, t]] += kappa[i] * alpha[i] * PE;
        ev[3-choice[i, t]] = 1 - ev[choice[i, t]];
        alpha[i] = eta[i] * abs(PE) + (1 - eta[i]) * alpha[i];
      }
    }
  }
}

Here's my YAML file for model information:

task_name:
  code: bandit2arm
  desc: 2-Armed Bandit Task
  cite:
    - "Li, J., Schiller, D., Schoenbaum, G., Phelps, E. A., & Daw, N. D. (2011).
      Differential roles of human striatum and amygdala in associative learning.
      Nature Neuroscience, 14(10), 1250-1252. https://doi.org/10.1038/nn.2904"
model_name:
  code: hybrid
  desc: Rescorla-Wagner (hybrid) Model
  cite: 
model_type:
  code:
  desc: Hierarchical
notes:
contributors:
data_columns:
  subjID: A unique identifier for each subject in the data-set.
  choice: "Integer value representing the option chosen on the given trial: 1 or 2."
  outcome:
    Integer value representing the outcome of the given trial (where reward
    == 1, and loss == 0).
parameters:
  alpha:
    desc: attention
    info: [0, 0.5, 1]
  kappa:
    desc: constraint
    info: [0, 0.5, 1]
  eta:
    desc: weight
    info: [0, 0.5, 1]
  tau:
    desc: inverse temperature
    info: [0, 1, 5]
regressors:
postpreds:
  - y_pred
additional_args:

Hi Zijie,

To contribute a new model to hBayesDM, I'm sorry that the contributor should have decent knowledge in Stan... we are busy with our own projects/schedules and cannot do it unless we collaborate on a project or so. Thanks for your understanding. Please check this wiki carefully, which shows how you can add a new task/model to hBayesDM. 

https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/wiki

Best,
Young
